thread:
sre-bot: ALERT: us-west-2 inference p95 latency > 1200ms for the last 5m on service 'runtime-ingest' :rotating_light:
maya: seeing it in Grafana too, p95 spike aligns with new runtime canary deploy 2026-05-12T22:03
jonathan: I rolled canary 2026-05-12 22:02 — the batching heuristics change (adaptive window) went out.
alex: logs show increased KV cache evictions on the canary nodes, memory pressure up ~30% on serving pods.
lisa: any 503s?
maya: error rate stable, just token latency. Throughput is similar.
oncall-rotation: tagging @jonathan and @alex — can we verify if adaptive batching is growing batch sizes beyond expected?
jonathan: yes, batch size distribution shifted from median 8->22 on long-tail requests after change. That plus more KV cache misses explains latency.
alex: reproducing locally with the canary config: when seq_len variations occur, adaptive window expands causing cache churn and backend stalls.
maya: mitigation options: rollback canary, force batch size cap, or disable prefix caching for canary. Thoughts on fastest rollback?
jonathan: rollback is safest. I'm preparing a rollback PR now. deploy-bot: Rolling back release runtime-adaptive-batching v3.4.1 -> v3.4.0 (canary) by request from jonathan.
deploy-bot: Rollback triggered: jobs started: kube rollout restart runtime-service-canary (pods will restart).
lisa: while rollback runs, can we divert new sessions away from us-west-2 or enable traffic-shed to eu-west temporarily?
maya: we have capacity in eu-west and us-east but redistributing could increase cross-region latency for users. For serving-critical customers we can failover.
alex: quick hotfix we tried in staging: set env `MAX_BATCH_SIZE=12` and `ENABLE_PREFIX_CACHE=false` — this reduces memory churn and keeps latency in check.
jonathan: hotfix would require changing canary config then promote if stable. But a full rollback will restore baseline faster.
oncall-rotation: what's the estimate for rollback completion?
deploy-bot: Rollback: 6/8 canary pods restarted, 2 remaining (pending due to node cordon). ETA ~2m.
maya: cordon issue due to transient k8s scheduling delay after node eviction — I've bumped node pool by +2 GPUs to help scheduling.
alex: after first rollback pod came back, p95 dropped from 1200ms -> 230ms on that instance.
jonathan: rollback complete. Monitoring...
deploy-bot: Rollback: complete. All canary pods running v3.4.0.
lisa: checking global metrics — p95 now trending down in us-west-2 to 300-400ms. Still elevated compared to baseline 200ms.
maya: action items: 1) open infra ticket to check node memory pressure pattern (maya) 2) revert adaptive batching change in feature branch and add stricter unit/regression tests for KV cache interplay (jonathan) 3) run targeted soak with long-tail seq_len distribution to validate batching (alex) 4) consider autoscale safety cap to prevent sudden batch size jumps (product discussion).
jonathan: will also add a runtime flag `ADAPTIVE_WINDOW_MAX=16` so future rollouts have a safe upper-bound.
oncall-rotation: cost note: temporarily bumping node pool by +2 GPUs may incur ~12% hourly overrun but avoids customer-impact. Approve?
lisa: approved. We need incident note for postmortem.
maya: filing incident now: INC-2026-0456 — I'll include timeline, Grafana links, and screenshots.
jonathan: adding PR link to revert: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3214
alex: follow-up: we should add a metric for KV cache eviction rate so alerts can catch this earlier.
maya: good call. I'll add it to alerting queue. :white_check_mark:
noncall-rotation: closing slack loop — reach out if p95 creeps back up, otherwise we'll move this to postmortem channel in 1h.
